data.text: The Data Science and Machine Learning Club at the University of Calgary hosts an annual competition to give students an opportunity to showcase their programming and data science skills. Open to university students, it provides a platform to demonstrate their abilities using a comprehensive dataset in front of the broader community. This competition involves data science tasks including visualization, manipulation, and analysis, applying classroom concepts to real-world data.

Participation in this competition allows students to gain recognition for their achievements, build their portfolios, and make valuable connections that support their career development in data science.

points.text: The inaugural competition attracted 37 attendees and 7 participants, with sponsorship from ARC Resources and a keynote by Dr. Xuewen Lu, bringing valuable academic insights.

In 2024, attendance more than doubled to 78 attendees, marking a 210% increase. Keynote speaker Renee Matsalla from Tacit Edge discussed data science in product management, enhancing the event’s industry relevance.

data.title: Competition Categories
descriptions: The competition is structured into three categories, allowing participants to compete in areas that best showcase their skills and interests.

bullets.title: Data Visualization
bullets.text: Focuses on creating compelling and informative visualizations that communicate insights and patterns in the data.

bullets.title: Machine Learning Approach
bullets.text: Involves applying machine learning algorithms, including data cleaning, pre-processing, algorithm selection, and results evaluation.

bullets.title: Research Proposal Approach
bullets.text: Encourages participants to formulate and present a research proposal based on data analysis, identifying trends and presenting a concise research question.

points.text: The competition begins with an official kickoff event where students are introduced to project guidelines, expectations, and the timeline.
During this phase, students work on constructing their projects, applying skills, conducting research, and collaborating to develop innovative solutions.
After project development, participants submit their final projects for evaluation by a panel of expert judges who assess innovation, technical execution, and impact.
Top teams present their projects at a live symposium with sponsors and industry professionals. Winners are announced, and awards are presented.

data.text: The competition culminates in an in-person symposium, where participants present their work to a panel of judges, peers, and industry professionals. This event provides a valuable networking opportunity, recognition for accomplishments, and experience in presenting work to a broader audience.
